tasks.short: Recommend a diagnostic or therapeutic intervention for this complaint.

steps.what: Hear the complaint that these interventions must address.
Write complaint, age and current medicines on the card.
Choose the protocol paragraph with attention to this complaint.
Draft lines for the diagnostic or therapeutic interventions she may recommend.

loop.input: The findings card from s2 and the protocol paragraph she chose in s3.
loop.output: Up to three option lines on an internal card. Each line quotes one clause of that paragraph.
loop.check: Every line quotes a clause from the chosen paragraph and names one of safety, cost, invasiveness, simplicity, acceptability, adherence or efficacy. A line that adds a dose, a test or an intervention the paragraph does not state fails.
loop.stop: One pass, at most three lines. If any line fails the check, the card stays blank and she writes the options.
loop.why_not_simpler: The paragraph is prose, not a table of those points, so a field copy cannot tell a safety clause from a line about something else.

steps.what: Judge which option fits safety, cost, invasiveness, simplicity, acceptability, adherence and efficacy.
Recommend the chosen diagnostic or therapeutic intervention to the patient.
Write the recommended intervention on the patient record.

tasks.design: She writes the complaint, age and current medicines on a card, and chooses the protocol paragraph in {DOCS}. A loop drafts option lines for the diagnostic or therapeutic interventions by quoting that paragraph onto an internal option card. She judges the lines and recommends one intervention herself, then writes it on the {OTHER} patient record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The points sit in prose, and a wrong recommendation can harm the patient.
tasks.enabler_now: A bounded draft can quote a protocol paragraph she has already chosen.
tasks.still_hard: Matching this complaint to the paragraph, and judging acceptability for this person.
tasks.human_edge: She is accountable for the recommendation and for what the patient will actually do.

ambition.what: On a visit whose protocol paragraph states adherence and acceptability, judge whether those two points rule out an otherwise effective option.

tasks.altitude: She still hears the complaint, still judges the points and still recommends the intervention. The week only loses a second reading of a paragraph she already chose. Prescribing rights do not move.

reach.learn: State safety, adherence and acceptability as clauses a quote can point at.

reach.task: Agree which paragraph covers this complaint
reach.learn: A blank option card is not a request to choose the intervention for her.

evidence.claim: A bounded draft that quotes a paragraph the clinician already chose is model knowledge. The digest does not measure this recommendation task.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner. A draft is not a prescription.
Solely automated care decisions need an article 22 basis, so she judges the option.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, and must assess, train, test and monitor it. The inspectorate names medication errors from wrong registration.

assumptions: This task is the recommendation for one complaint. She writes the patient record herself. The option card is internal and is not written onto the record by the loop.

She produces the findings card in s2, with complaint, age and current medicines, before the loop. She produces the choice of protocol paragraph in s3. The paragraph text is the clinic protocol in {DOCS}. Producer is the protocol owner. If she has not chosen a paragraph, the loop does not run and she writes the options. That earlier protocol authoring is not this task's saving.

No ambient microphone. Hearing, choosing, judging, recommending and writing the record stay at full time. The one hour per 100 baseline hours is a monthly sample of option lines for a clause the paragraph does not state. The published note-time study is not this saving.
Where the digest names Dutch rules, the named-practitioner rule and the bar on solely automated care decisions apply. Elsewhere, national rules apply.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's protocol paragraphs already state safety, adherence and acceptability as quotable clauses.
Whether a works council must consent before an edit log is kept on the option card.
research_questions: Which protocol paragraphs in this clinic already separate safety, adherence and acceptability into clauses a quote can point at?

already_counted.description: Judging the quoted lines against the paragraph and the findings card.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of option lines for a clause the chosen paragraph does not state.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The draft runs only when she has already chosen a protocol paragraph. Otherwise she writes the options and the saving is zero. Hearing, choosing, judging, recommending and writing the record stay at full time. One hour per 100 baseline hours is the monthly sample. The published note-time study is not applied. High stays below the net of 7.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Detect an adverse drug reaction and respond with the patient.

steps.what: Read the stored drug name, dose and patient group.
Copy a stored interaction line onto an internal card.
Detect adverse reactions in infants, children, pregnant or lactating women, and older adults.
Write the symptom, the drug and the vulnerable populations with special attention.
Decide if this is an adverse reaction and the response.
Respond to that reaction with the patient in the room.
Record the reaction and the response on the patient record.

tasks.design: She reads the medicine row on the {OTHER} patient record. Where the drug name matches, the stored interaction sentence from {DOCS} is copied onto an internal card. She detects adverse reactions in the room, decides the response, carries it out, and records the reaction herself on the {OTHER} patient record.
tasks.previous_blocker: A reaction is seen in the room, and a vulnerable group is not a code on the row.
tasks.enabler_now: An interaction sentence for a named drug can be copied once the drug name is already stored.
tasks.still_hard: Seeing the reaction and choosing the response, especially for infants, pregnancy and older adults.
tasks.human_edge: She decides whether this is an adverse reaction, and she carries out the response, including any change to the medicine.
tasks.altitude: She still watches the patient, still decides whether a reaction has occurred and still carries out the response. The week only loses retyping an interaction sentence that was already stored. Any change to the medicine stays her decision.

reach.task: Store the medicine row before the visit
reach.learn: Drug name, dose and patient group must already be on the row or the copy does not run.

reach.task: Keep the interaction sentence on the reference extract
reach.learn: One sentence per drug name, matched on that name, before the visit.

evidence.claim: The G-Standaard checks interactions, contraindications, doses and duplicates, and KNMP sets the content. It does not see a clinical reaction in the room.
The inspectorate names medication errors from wrong registration as a reason to be careful with generative tools.
A prescription, including a change to a medicine, comes from a named practitioner. A copied sentence does not make that change.
Solely automated care decisions need an article 22 basis. She decides the response.

assumptions: This task is the visit where she watches for an adverse reaction and responds. The copy writes an internal card only. She records the reaction and the response herself. The card does not change the dose.

The prescribing practitioner has already stored drug name, dose and patient group on the medicine row of the {OTHER} patient record. The pharmacist has already stored drug name and one interaction sentence on the reference extract in {DOCS}. If the drug name is missing, or no sentence matches that name, the copy step does not run and she looks the interaction up inside the decision. That earlier capture is not this task's saving.

No ambient microphone. Watching, deciding, responding and recording stay at full time. Incremental hours are zero because the copy is an exact sentence with no model to maintain. Reading the card while she decides is already inside the decision step.
Where the digest names Dutch rules, the named-practitioner rule applies to any change she makes to the medicine. Elsewhere, national rules apply.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's medicine row already stores drug name, dose and patient group before she sees the patient.
Whether the reference extract holds one interaction sentence per drug name, or only a code.
research_questions: On what share of visits is the drug name already on the medicine row before she starts this task?

already_counted.description: Reading the copied interaction line while deciding the response.

incremental.description: No standing upkeep. The copy is an exact sentence already stored, and there is no model to maintain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The copy runs only when the medicine row already has a drug name that matches a stored sentence. Otherwise she looks the interaction up inside the decision and the saving is zero. Watching, deciding, responding and recording stay at full time. Incremental hours are zero. High stays below the net of 4.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Diagnose and treat an acute illness, infection or injury.

steps.what: Examine the acute illness, infection or injury.
Diagnose the acute health problems from the exam.
Treat the acute illnesses, infections or injuries in the room.
Write the diagnosis and the treatment she gave.
Draft the visit sentence from that diagnosis line.

loop.input: The diagnosis and treatment line she wrote in s4. No exam feed and no medicine code.
loop.check: The sentence restates only the diagnosis and the treatment on that line. It adds no new diagnosis, dose, test or medicine.
loop.stop: One pass, one sentence. If the line is missing or the check fails, the draft stays blank, she writes the sentence, and the filing step does not run.
loop.why_not_simpler: The line is free text, so a fixed template cannot tell her diagnosis from a word that only looks like one.

steps.what: Check the visit sentence states only that diagnosis line.
File the confirmed visit sentence on the patient record.

tasks.design: She examines, diagnoses and treats the acute problem, then writes the diagnosis and the treatment on one line. A loop drafts one visit sentence from that line only. After she checks it, a separate step files the confirmed sentence on the {OTHER} patient record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The acute diagnosis and the treatment cannot be written before the exam.
tasks.enabler_now: Once she has written the line, one sentence can be drafted, and filed only after she checks it.
tasks.still_hard: The exam, the diagnosis and the treatment in the room.
tasks.human_edge: She is the named practitioner for the treatment she gives.
tasks.altitude: She still examines, diagnoses and treats. The week only loses retyping one sentence from a line she already wrote, and only after she has checked it. She remains the named practitioner for the treatment.

reach.task: State what a visit sentence may repeat
reach.learn: The sentence may repeat only the diagnosis line she wrote. It is not a test order.

reach.task: Read the next visit from the record
reach.learn: Read the filed sentence, not the draft.

evidence.claim: Autoscriber records the consultation, the clinician validates, and the note can be stored in the patient record.
The patient dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.
A prescription comes from a named practitioner. The filed sentence is not a prescription.
Solely automated care decisions need an article 22 basis. She confirms the sentence before it is filed.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, and must assess, train, test and monitor it.
Ambient recording that captures staff performance needs works-council consent, so this task types the line and does not record the consult.

assumptions: This task is the acute exam, the diagnosis and the treatment. The machine acts are only the draft of one visit sentence and, after she confirms it, the filing of that sentence. Any prescription she issues is inside the treatment step, and it is hers.

She produces the diagnosis line in s4 before the draft. The line states the diagnosis and the treatment she gave. If the line is missing, or the draft is blank, she writes the sentence and the filing step does not run.
Filing stores only the confirmed text from s6. A later edit of the diagnosis line voids the confirmation. The filed sentence is not a prescription and not a test order.

No ambient microphone. Works-council consultation still applies to edit logs on the filed sentence. The one hour per 100 baseline hours is a monthly sample of filed sentences for a line the diagnosis note does not support. The published note-time study is not applied.
Where the digest names Dutch rules, the twenty-year dossier and the named-practitioner rule apply. Elsewhere, national rules apply.
unknowns: Whether a nurse practitioner may file this visit sentence on this record without a physician countersignature.
Whether the works council has already consented to edit logs on care notes.
research_questions: What share of acute visits in this clinic already end with one diagnosis line the nurse practitioner wrote herself?

already_counted.description: Checking the visit sentence against the diagnosis line before it is filed.

incremental.description: Monthly sample of filed sentences for a line the diagnosis note does not support.

approvals.approved_version: Visit sentence for this patient and this acute problem, as the nurse practitioner confirmed it repeats only the diagnosis and treatment line she wrote. A later edit of that line voids this confirmation. The filed sentence is not a prescription and not a test order.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The draft and the filing run only when she has written a diagnosis line and then confirmed the sentence. A blank draft means she writes the sentence and the filing step does not run. Exam, diagnosis, treatment and the check stay at full time. One hour per 100 baseline hours is the monthly sample. The published note-time study is not applied. High stays below the net of 5.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Counsel patients on regimens, side effects and other substances.

steps.what: Hear the drug regimens and the other substances patients use.
Write the regimen, supplements, medications and herbal remedies.
Choose the vetted paragraph for this drug regimen.
Fill quote lines for those effects and interactions.
Check each quote names only a substance she wrote.
Counsel patients about possible side effects and interactions.

tasks.design: She writes the regimens and the other substances, and chooses the vetted paragraph in {DOCS}. A fill step copies sentences from that paragraph that name a substance she wrote onto an internal quote card. She checks the quotes, then counsels the patients herself.
tasks.previous_blocker: Side-effect counsel is a conversation, and a leaflet sentence is not advice for this patient.
tasks.enabler_now: Quote lines can be filled from a paragraph she chose, and only for substances she wrote.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing what the patient actually takes, and saying what the leaflet does not cover.
tasks.human_edge: She counsels the person, and she adds the warning the card left blank.
tasks.altitude: She still hears what the patient takes and still counsels in the room. The week only loses copying leaflet sentences that name a substance she already wrote. Advice the leaflet does not cover stays hers.

reach.learn: The paragraph must name side effects and interactions in words the fill can match to a substance she wrote.

reach.task: Leave personal advice with the clinician
reach.learn: A quote card is not counsel. She still speaks to the patient.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts is vetted guideline text. An answer can cite its paragraph, and personal advice stays with the clinician.
Providers must know whether a generative tool is a medical device, and must assess, train, test and monitor it. The inspectorate names medication errors from wrong registration.
Solely automated care decisions need an article 22 basis. She counsels the patient herself.

assumptions: This task is the counsel conversation. The fill writes an internal quote card. The card is not written to the patient record. She counsels the patient herself.

She produces the substance list in s2 before the fill: regimen, supplements, medications and herbal remedies, in the words the patient used. She chooses the leaflet paragraph in s3. The paragraph is vetted text in {DOCS}. Producer is the pharmacist or the guideline owner. The fill copies a sentence only when that paragraph contains a substance string she wrote. Other lines stay blank and she says them while counseling. If she has not chosen a paragraph, the fill does not run.

No ambient microphone and no patient-facing bot. Hearing, choosing, checking and counseling stay at full time. Incremental hours are zero because the fill is an exact string copy with no model to maintain. Checking the quotes is already inside the check step.
Where the digest names Dutch rules, solely automated care decisions stay barred. Elsewhere, national rules apply. The published note-time study is not this saving.
unknowns: Whether this clinic's leaflet paragraphs are already vetted for side effects, supplements and herbal remedies.
How often the patient's name for a herbal remedy is absent from the paragraph, so the line stays blank.
research_questions: Do the vetted paragraphs name supplements and herbal remedies in the words patients use, or only in catalogue names?

already_counted.description: Checking each quote against a substance she wrote.

incremental.description: No standing upkeep. The fill is an exact string copy, and there is no model to maintain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The fill runs only when the paragraph she chose contains a substance string she wrote. Unmatched lines stay blank and she says them while counseling. Hearing, choosing, checking and counseling stay at full time. Incremental hours are zero. High stays below the net of 6.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still the clinic list. She still diagnoses, treats, counsels and responds in the room. The only change is an internal option card, a copied interaction line on an internal card, a visit sentence she confirms before it is filed, and leaflet quotes on an internal card. Prescribing and any change to a medicine stay hers.
reach: Pharmacist: keep the drug name and the interaction sentence on the reference extract before the copy runs.
Prescribing practitioner: store drug name, dose and patient group on the medicine row before the visit.
Protocol owner: state safety, adherence and acceptability as clauses a quote can point at.
Family medicine physician: state which diagnosis line is enough for the visit sentence.
skills_to_grow: Check that a drafted option line quotes the protocol paragraph and does not add a dose.
Name the vulnerable group on a reaction note.
Confirm a visit sentence repeats only the diagnosis line before it is filed.
Keep counsel to the leaflet sentence, and speak any substance the card left blank.
role.ambitious_version: On a visit where the protocol states adherence, she judges that point before she recommends, and the visit sentence on the record is one she has already confirmed.
